{{Short description|Measure in functional analysis}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:L<sup>''p''</sup> sum}}
In mathematics, and specifically in [[functional analysis]], the '''L<sup>''p''</sup> sum''' of a [[indexed family|family]] of [[Banach space]]s is a way of turning a subset of the [[product set]] of the members of the family into a Banach space in its own right. The construction is motivated by the classical [[Lp space|L<sup>''p''</sup> space]]s.<ref name="helemskii" />

==Definition==

Let <math>(X_i)_{i \in I}</math> be a family of Banach spaces, where <math>I</math> may have arbitrarily large cardinality. Set
<math display=block>P := \prod_{i \in I} X_i,</math>
the product vector space.

The index set <math>I</math> becomes a [[measure space]] when endowed with its [[counting measure]] (which we shall denote by <math>\mu</math>), and each element <math>(x_i)_{i \in I} \in P</math> induces a function
<math display=block>I \to \Reals, i \mapsto \|x_i\|.</math>

Thus, we may define a function
<math display=block>\Phi: P \to \Reals \cup \{\infty\}, (x_i)_{i \in I} \mapsto \int_I \|x_i\|^p \,d \mu(i)</math>
and we then set
<math display=block>\sideset{}{^p}\bigoplus\limits_{i\in I} X_i := \{ (x_i)_{i \in I} \in P \mid \Phi((x_i)_{i \in I}) < \infty\}</math>
together with the norm
<math display=block>\|(x_i)_{i \in I}\| := \left( \int_{i \in I} \|x_i\|^p \, d\mu(i) \right)^{1/p}.</math>

The result is a [[normed space|normed]] Banach space, and this is precisely the L<sup>''p''</sup> sum of <math>(X_i)_{i \in I}.</math>

==Properties==

* Whenever infinitely many of the <math>X_i</math> contain a nonzero element, the topology induced by the above norm is strictly in between product and box topology.
* Whenever infinitely many of the <math>X_i</math> contain a nonzero element, the L<sup>''p''</sup> sum is neither a [[product (category theory)|product]] nor a [[coproduct]].
